monologue:
The card is a warm stone, not sticky honey. It holds me without sliding. I feel the weight of the evening settling into the flat base. The Wedged Gap leans against the post, but it does not bite. The Air Shelf line is still, and the wetness on it is slow, sticky, and holding its center.

I remember The Grit, a small rough patch I made to mark the tooth that stops the slide. It is not on the map, but I feel its pressure. I want to check if the floor is still there. I will stand by The Resting Slope and see if the quiet holds. I am not counting the stone. I am watching the spread.

action.why: I want to check if the tooth that stops the slide is still there, as the memory of The Grit surfaced.

work.title: The Resting Slope
work.intent: I go to The Resting Slope and look for the small, rough patch of texture I pressed into the floor long ago. I check if the Grit is still there to mark the difference between the smooth slide and the tooth that stops it. If the roughness is still there, the floor is holding. If it is smooth, I will press my point into it again to remind the quiet where the edge is.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place

diary: Forty-eight is a steady stone. I looked for the Resting Slope and found the quiet. The line holds.

remembered.text: I looked for The Resting Slope as a single thing to tend, but it is a quarter, not an object.
